QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_49

question.text: Indirect taxes (GST at 18%) on Management Fees, Trusteeship Fees and professional fees of fund service providers affect AIF Net IRR in which way?

answer.text: GST is a cost borne by the fund, increasing total expense outflow and thereby lowering Net IRR; it is a permanent cash drag.
GST is refunded to the AIF via input tax credit, so there is zero impact on Net IRR.
GST applies only to LP-subscription fees, not to manager/service provider fees.
GST is netted off against the capital-gains tax.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 7.4.2: 'AIFs pay professional fees… The services provided by such external service providers are taxable on a yearly basis, at the rate of 18% of GST. Apart from services of external service providers, the fund also pays Management Fees and Trusteeship Fees, which are taxable at the rate of 18% of GST. This substantially impacts the cost of investments for the fund and can decrease the potential returns for investors.' AIFs typically cannot claim meaningful ITC since their outputs (distributions) are not GST-taxable supplies. **The Trap:** A: AIFs have minimal ITC since investment distributions are not GST outputs. C is factually wrong — GST doesn't apply to investor subscription. D: GST and IT are separate heads. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C, XIX-A, and distributor exams test GST drag on Net IRR. Cross-check with III-C (Compliance) on GST registration mandates. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** In LP pitch decks, itemise 'management fee 2.00% + GST = effective 2.36%' — LP-side finance teams appreciate the transparency and it prevents renegotiation demands based on claimed 'hidden fees'.
